findings.passage: “Coloradans should be able to cast their ballots without fear or intimidation. Deploying armed guards at postal facilities just as voting begins demands an explanation and urgent action,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen.
findings.note: Press release in her name about her letter to the Postal Inspection Service on armed guards at postal facilities where voters may drop off mail ballots. Related to mail-voting access, not to ID or citizenship rules. The memo it describes has guards checking IDs of people at postal sites, not voters.
subjects: mail voting access and voter intimidation

findings.passage: Colorado has one of the most accessible and most secure voting systems in the country. I’m disappointed — but not surprised — that Republicans unanimously opposed my amendment to make sure millions aren’t kicked off voter rolls.
findings.note: Pettersen's press statement after the House Rules Committee rejected her amendment to the SAVE Act, issued the day the House passed the bill. She describes Colorado's voting system and the amendment's aim of keeping eligible voters on the rolls.

findings.passage: Requiring in-person voter registration, in addition to more paperwork, will make voting exceptionally hard for working women and women with caregiving responsibilities.
findings.note: From the fact list in her office's release on the SAVE Act. It also says about 69 million women have IDs that do not match their birth certificates because of a name change.
subjects: documents that must match a voter's name

findings.motion: Pettersen amendment to the SAVE Act offered in House Rules Committee (rejected)
findings.note: Her office's release says the amendment would have delayed the bill's start until all state election officials certify that it will not reduce voting access. The release says Rules Committee members unanimously opposed it.
